evidence.mechanism: shot-02s: a rust run of diagonals sits left of the marker at x~236 while ochre bars sit right of it; by shot-08s the marker has moved to x~308 and the colour boundary has shifted with it.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one flat 2D line truss of about 30 panels plus a single influence-line plot underneath; no depth, material or layered rendering, so it is one rendering idea on one solver.
evidence.craft: shot-20s: clean cream ground with even 1px chords and evenly sized diagonals and no artefacts; the influence-line plot has a hard vertical step at midspan and the bars read thin at full size.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: cream, ochre and rust palette with force-sign colouring on a line truss matches no anchor; anchor-12 shares warm tones, but its orrery and spiral overlap nothing shown here.
evidence.polish: shot-20s: the full span pulls back with the marker parked at the right end, which resolves the piece; but the frame reads close to shot-02s, so development is mostly marker travel.

pairwise_justification: No median archive yet: the median block reads NONE, so the head-to-head check is skipped.

critique.change: Add a second developing layer to the truss: give each diagonal a force-magnitude glow or thickness that changes as the marker moves, so shot-08s and shot-20s differ in more than colour.
Make shot-20s a settled end state, not a near copy of shot-02s: leave a residual pattern of rust centre bars and ochre ends on screen after the marker exits.
Mark each zero-crossing on screen: when a diagonal's force crosses zero, flash its joint and draw a tick on the influence-line plot at the same x, linking the flip to the bar that caused it.
